explanation: Recursively materialize inorder as left-subtree values, current value, and right-subtree values. Require every adjacent pair in that complete array to be strictly increasing. The recursive array construction may repeatedly copy values.
timeComplexity: O(n squared) worst-case time: recursive inorder concatenation copies subtree values repeatedly along a skew tree; the final comparison or indexed lookup adds at most O(n).
spaceComplexity: O(n+h) live auxiliary values and recursion frames for n nodes and height h. Completed sibling results and partial inorder arrays together hold O(n) values; cumulative allocation/copying can be quadratic.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: For any binary tree, the strict BST property is equivalent to strictly increasing inorder values. Inorder places all left descendants before their ancestor and all right descendants after it. Any nonincreasing adjacent pair proves an ordering violation; if every pair increases, every subtree has the required global ordering.
walkthrough: For [7,3,10,1,8], inorder values are [1,3,8,7,10]. The decrease from 8 to 7 shows that 8 lies incorrectly inside the root’s left subtree. Return false, even though 8 exceeds its immediate parent 3.
edgeCases: Duplicate keys are invalid in this strict BST contract.
Checking only direct parent-child comparisons misses ancestor violations.
